newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury romps ahead on bumper sales news.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury romps ahead on bumper sales news.

text.p: Shares in J. Sainsbury Plc advanced on Wednesday after better-than-expected trading news released at today's shareholders' meeting.
Sainsbury said 16-week sales rose 4.2 percent on a like-for-like basis.
"Basically it is good news, ahead of market expectations, and ours, at 3-3/4 percent," said one specialist salesman.
The shares rose 13p to 401p after the news having traded 5p higher beforehand.
Other supermarket groups rose in Sainsbury's wake. Safeway Plc was 15-1/2p up at 390-1/2p, helped earlier by a recommendation from analysts at SocGen to switch from Sainsbury into Safeway.
Tesco climbed 16-1/2p to 425p and Marks and Spencer rose 20p to 528p.

Lifting the sector earlier was the view that food retail stocks continued to benefit from a flight to safety after the budget, and as currency sensitive stocks were dogged by the prospect of further interest rate rises.
"This sector has shone as they have absolutely no problems with strong sterling and they are unaffected by the change in dividend tax," said one senior dealer.
"News yesterday that inflation was picking up was also good for these stocks," he said.
